title: Man and monkey IT
blurb: The same 92 photographs shown to people in a scanner and to monkeys with electrodes in inferior temporal cortex. Each view is how differently that brain region responds to every pair of images.
metricNote: Both views are correlation distance as published, 1 − Pearson r between the response patterns two images evoke: across 316 IT voxels for people (averaged over eight sessions), across 674 IT neurons for monkeys.

about.name: Matching Categorical Object Representations in Inferior Temporal Cortex of Man and Monkey
about.quote: Here, we presented monkeys and humans with the same images of real-world objects and measured the IT response pattern elicited by each image. In order to relate the representations between the species and to computational models, we compare response-pattern dissimilarity matrices. IT response patterns form category clusters, which match between man and monkey.
about.label: Neuron

about.name: Object Category Structure in Response Patterns of Neuronal Population in Monkey Inferior Temporal Cortex
about.quote: We found that the categorical structure of objects is represented by the pattern of activity distributed over the cell population. Animate and inanimate objects created distinguishable clusters in the population code.
about.label: Journal of Neurophysiology

here: Here: all 92 images, as the human-IT dissimilarity matrix of the paper’s Fig. 1, averaged over two fMRI sessions in each of four people (A), and the monkey-IT one from 674 neurons in two macaques (B). Both are 1 − Pearson r between response patterns, taken from the RSA toolbox’s copy of the paper’s supplemental data. The object names are ours.
